title: Sequenced diff applier for analytics backfill with rate-limited recovery lane
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Build a sequenced, idempotent diff-applier service to apply ordered deltas to analytics projections and metrics stores when upstream event corrections or schema migrations occur. The tool will perform incremental patch application in a 'rate-limited recovery lane' to avoid saturation of online query/ingest systems and preserve SLOs for the Console. Core responsibilities: ensure strict ordering per-entity key, provide durable checkpointing, support dry-run verification, expose canary windows, and integrate safety heuristics for schema drift and anomaly throttling.
acceptance_criteria: Service can apply ordered diffs to the metrics projection store with exactly-once semantics for a given shard when diffs are delivered at-least-once
Checkpointing and resume: any worker restart resumes from last applied sequence id for its owned shards
Rate-limited recovery lane enforces cluster-level token bucket so backfills do not increase API tail latency beyond configured SLOs
Dry-run mode produces a PATCH plan report and checksum that matches a non-destructive preview run against a snapshot dataset
Canary rollout: support running on 1% entity key range and show end-to-end dashboards before wider rollout
Operational dashboards for throughput, apply-failures, conflicts, and estimated remaining time
Automated safety stop triggers when conflict rate or error rate exceeds thresholds and notifies SRE/PM via Slack and PagerDuty
implementation_steps: Design protocol for ordered diffs: sequence id per entity, vector for cross-entity causal ordering where required
Storage layout: per-shard durable checkpoint in Redis or DynamoDB with write-ahead log for applied sequence ids
Worker model: shard ownership via leader-election, lease renewal, and graceful handoff
Rate-limit lane: cluster-global token bucket with adjustable burst and priority lanes (user-facing requests > recovery lane)
Idempotency: use deterministic patch IDs and pre-check applied sequence to skip duplicates
Conflict handling: three-tier strategy: (1) fast-merge for commutative operations, (2) tombstone-and-rewrite for incompatible schema changes, (3) manual review queue for semantic conflicts
Dry-run engine: replay diffs against a sandbox projection and emit detailed per-diff diffs and hashes
Canary & rollout automation: job that seeds diffs for a small key-range and compares metrics against baseline
Integrations: link with Console Observability (trace headers), Redwood Optimize recommendations for throttle tuning, and audit logs for compliance
progress_notes: 2025-02-17: Kickoff meeting with Metrics, Console Backend, and SRE. Agreed on per-entity ordering and Redis leases for fast checkpointing.

2025-02-21: Spike completed: prototype applied sequences to a local metrics sqlite snapshot. Discovered high conflict rate for aggregated counters when applying out-of-order diffs — added requirement for commutative patch ops.
2025-02-26: Design review with PM and SRE. Decided to prioritize a rate-limited recovery lane and integrate token-bucket with existing API rate-limiter to prevent resource contention.
2025-03-01: Implemented durable checkpointing and shard leasing MVP. End-to-end unit tests for resume semantics added.

2025-03-03: Canary dry-run executed against 1% partition. Patch plan report matched expected checksums. Observed 12% CPU increase on projection nodes; SRE recommends reducing recovery lane burst from 500 to 150 tokens.
2025-03-04: Added safety stop: abort and create manual review ticket when persistent apply error ratio > 1% for 5 minutes. PR opened for safety stop logic (github.com/redwood/console/pull/4821).
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Using Redis for checkpointing gives low latency but requires careful failover planning; alternate option was DynamoDB for stronger durability but higher tail latency — chose Redis with periodic durable snapshots
Rate-limited recovery lane reduces total backfill throughput but prevents SLO regressions for customer-facing requests — accepted for safety
Conflict-handling favors automatic fast-merge where safe; manual review is more expensive but required for ambiguous semantic changes
Chosen worker model uses lease-based shard ownership to simplify handoff; this can lead to temporary lag during leader churn but reduces cross-shard coordination complexity
review_feedback: PM (Sofia Alvarez): asked for clearer UX in Console to start/stop backfills and exposed ETA — added requirement to Console backend APIs
SRE (Liam O'Connor): requested hard caps and circuit-breaker metrics; added safety stop and Prometheus metrics for token-bucket headroom
Design (Ivy Park): suggested a diff visualization in the dry-run report to help reviewers sign off on canary runs
Security (Rina Kapoor): requested audit log entries for all applied patches and dry-run exports — integrated into design
